title: SparseX: Efficient Segment-Level KV Cache Sharing for Interleaved LLM Serving
summary_zh: SparseX 針對「非前綴、跨請求、跨輪次、跨 agent」的分散重複片段提出片段級 KV cache 共享。它明確指出同一段文字在不同前綴下 K/V 會不同（前綴耦合），並把重用視為「一個依賴上下文與位置的近似計算問題」。核心機制是 SparseQ：以自然出現在重用工作負載中的非重用（接收端）query 作為探針，估計出哪些被重用 token 對當前輸出最重要，再對這些 top-k token 做 Sparse-KV 重算；其餘重用 token 只做 RoPE 對齊。搭配 full+sparse 混合注意力（早期層 full、邊界層選 token、後期層 sparse）。修正是純加法式（重算 / 重對齊），沒有任何減法式去污染，也不使用 contamination 一詞。與我方論點最接近：它做了 per-token、接收端相關性的選擇，但修正算子仍是重算而非減去污染。
summary_en: SparseX proposes segment-level KV cache sharing for repeated content that appears as non-prefix, cross-request, cross-turn, and cross-agent segments. It states our premise almost verbatim: the KV of the same segment differs under different prefixes (prefix coupling), so reuse is 'a context-dependent and position-dependent approximate computation problem.' The core mechanism is SparseQ: it uses the non-reuse (receiver) query positions that arise naturally in reuse workloads as a probe to estimate which reused tokens matter most to the current output, then applies Sparse-KV Recomputation to those top-k tokens while the rest are only RoPE-aligned; a full+sparse hybrid defers selection past the early layers. The repair is purely additive (recompute / re-align) with no subtractive decontamination, and it never names 'contamination'. Closest paper to our premise: it does per-token, receiver-relevance selection, but its correction operator recomputes rather than subtracts a contaminant.
